So, I really intended this sub to be welcoming to those struggling with all types of addictions (behavioral, substance, what have you) and all forms of recovery (religious, secular, psychotherapeutic, other).

However, I wanted to ask YOU - the charter members of AddictionRecovery, since this is YOUR group. Should we include "moderation" approaches here? And yes, they do have support groups, and they do have a "big book" of their own, believe it or not - check out this link if you want more information.

I do not endorse moderation approaches. I've tried them myself, they didn't work for me, and I will happily share why they don't work for me. Does that mean they don't work for others? Not for me to say, really - and I'm willing to believe that they may work for SOMEONE....

But the real question is - is formal discussion of moderation outside the scope of this group? Is attempting moderation the same thing as "recovery"?

I attend Lifering Secular Recovery, and I'm very enthusiastic about it. We have a very "universalist" philosophy about recovery - an attitude I'm trying to emulate here - which is why we typically have dedicated 12-step attendees amongst our ranks as well as a number of longtime members who've never set foot in "the rooms" in their lives and never intend to. However, what we don't compromise on is this: sobriety is our #1 goal. If you want to practice moderation and learn about how to do that, there are other groups for that.

Should that be our attitude here? Again, I'm not 100% decided on this, and I'm happy to let the group decide. Again, this is your sub, and your group.

Thanks for being here.
AddictionRecovery welcomes all forms of recovery... but should we formally include moderation approaches here? YOUR INPUT NEEDED

I think it is important to include all options for what helps people get sober. I know from working in a harm reduction agency that some people are able to moderate and eventually stop all together. I realize this approach is usually looked down upon in some aspects but if it is something that is helping another individual get help and sober then why should we stop them from talking about it?

I tend to think there are any number of paths towards successful, sustained recovery from addiction and I absolutely believe that some people need to practice controlled drinking / drugging, moderation, or whatnot before they get to the point where they can give it up completely. I know I did - obviously in certain ways I wish I had gone the abstinence route earlier, but on the other hand - I needed to try to do it my way first. Like many of us. :-)
I didn't realize the importance of harm reduction/moderation at first but after working for an agency with a harm reduction agency it really did teach me alot.
